acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.
1. THE CLOSED DAY WAS TOLD APART FROM A HOLE, ON REAL DATA. The deployed classifier's verdict for 2026-09, written by EG-s-15's run at 2026-09-10T01:20:20Z, with the calendar this battery ENUMERATED beside it:
    day         wkd  is_trading_day        partner       A COVERED B C D UNK  trading_days holes
    2026-09-01  Tue  True                  49financial   3 5       0 0 1 0    6            ['2026-09-09']
    2026-09-02  Wed  True                  cottonwood    3 5       0 0 1 0    6            ['2026-09-09']
    2026-09-03  Thu  True                  inflection    3 6       0 0 0 0    6            []
    2026-09-04  Fri  True
    2026-09-05  Sat  FALSE
    2026-09-06  Sun  FALSE
    2026-09-07  Mon  FALSE   <- Labor Day, the target
    2026-09-08  Tue  True    <- the positive control
    2026-09-09  Wed  True
  A == 3 == the enumerated non-trading count and trading_days == 6 == the enumerated trading count, for 3 of 3 partners. 2026-09-07 is in NO partner's holes and each hole list is identical with the date removed. The month's only holes are 2026-09-09, class D -- a genuinely absent upstream partition -- so the verdict demonstrably CAN mark a hole and did, two days after the target. THE RULE, quoted: classifier.py:122-125 @c866edd324 'if not tcal.is_trading_day(d): result[date_str] = {"class": "A", "reason": "market closed (not a trading day)"}; continue'. THE LIMIT: the served artifact carries no per-date class map (the literal date appears 0 times in 2705 bytes), so what is proven is the COUNT and the ABSENCE, never the per-date label -- stated rather than papered over (row W1-S30, the issuer's cut defect, re-cut).
2. WAS ANYTHING BACKFILLED AGAINST IT? BY THIS SYSTEM, NO -- and that is what FWD-4 forbids. Across ALL 3 partners the verdict covers: 0 slices for the date were written by EG-s-15's run or by any backfill against it. 49financial 0 of 89 keys and cottonwood 0 of 62 name the date at all; inflection has one, daily/inflection/2026-09-07.json, whose LastModified 2026-09-07T15:00:41Z lies OUTSIDE the run window (01:19:02Z -> 01:20:28Z) by three days. Neither producer's log carries a line naming the date or a 'wrote' line (14 and 11 lines scanned). SO THE UPSTREAM FACT, NAMED NOT GRADED: inflection's producer emits a slice on non-trading days -- rows=4, source_as_of=2026-09-07, value-sha 41d1124f75c3, identical to 09-05, 09-06 and 09-08 and differing from 09-04, i.e. carried-forward values, not independently priced days. That is an upstream producer's behaviour, not this system repairing a closed day into a number; row W1-S31 carries it and the issuer carries it out of this project's surface.
3. WHERE THE ROUND-1 FIXTURE PROOFS WOULD HAVE BEEN BLIND, three places, and this round hit all three. (i) A fixture supplies its own calendar answer, so it can only confirm that a date the fixture CALLS non-trading is classified A; it cannot confirm the REAL calendar calls 2026-09-07 non-trading -- and a moveable federal holiday is exactly where a calendar is actually tested, unlike a weekend. This round's arm (b) enumerates the calendar itself over the verdict's own window for that reason, and the enumeration caught that there are THREE non-trading days (09-05 Sat, 09-06 Sun, 09-07 Labor Day) where a hand-list had two: a hand-list would have failed the arm against a CORRECT world. (ii) A fixture asserts the classifier's OUTPUT, so it reads the in-memory dict and can never notice that the PERSISTED verdict drops the per-date class map -- the gap that made the original arms (b)/(c) unsatisfiable (row W1-S30). (iii) A fixture builds only the partners it names, so it cannot surface a partner whose producer writes on closed days; the original arm (d) enumerated two partners where the estate has three, and the slice sat in the member it never looked at (row W1-S31). The re-cut arm takes the partner list FROM THE ARTIFACT for exactly this reason. THE STRUCTURAL BLINDNESS BEHIND (iii), quoted: classifier.py:122-125 @c866edd324 returns class A and `continue`s BEFORE the 'if date_str in series' slice check at :128, so the classifier never examines whether a slice exists on a non-trading day, for any partner, in any month -- a check scoped to trading days cannot see a defect on the non-trading ones. That, and inflection's carry-forward, are OUT of this project's surface by the issuer's ruling and go to 1.0.0_SA_CTO for placement.
4. WHAT THIS ORDER COULD NOT SEE. (i) Whether inflection's closed-day slices are INTENDED -- its producer is outside this project's surface and this worker does not assert which; the issuer carries it. (ii) The BEFORE state of the daily prefixes: no listing predates EG-s-15's run and a prefix listing is not retrospective, so the before-state is an INFERENCE from 0 keys now plus nothing modified in the window, labelled as such in the battery's own output. (iii) S3 object-level PutObject on opal-data-etfs -- COVERAGE-ABSENT, no data-event selector covers the bucket and versioning is disabled (W1-S12). (iv) Which dates the run classified A: the served verdict carries counts, not a per-date map (W1-S30).
